learn: A good conversation has a greeting, questions, answers and a goodbye.
Useful starters: ¿Qué tal? (how's it going?), ¿Qué hay de nuevo? (what's new?), ¿Cómo te fue? (how did it go?).
Fillers like pues (well) and bueno (okay) give you time to think.
check: Pues is a word that means...
A good conversation ends with a...
lessons.try: Hold a two-minute conversation with a partner without using English.

learn: Show interest: ¡Qué bien! (how great!), ¡Qué lástima! (what a shame!), ¿De verdad? (really?).
Ask follow-up questions: ¿Por qué? (why?), ¿Y después? (and then?).
Porque means because. Listen for ¿por qué? and answer porque...
lessons.try: Practice answering five ¿por qué? questions with porque.

learn: Use usted with adults you do not know well: ¿Me puede ayudar? (can you help me?).
Con permiso means excuse me when passing by. Perdón means sorry for bumping someone.
¡Que tenga un buen día! means have a nice day.
lessons.try: Role-play speaking to a shopkeeper using usted.
React to five pieces of news.
Ask three follow-up questions in a chat.
Debate the best pet politely.

learn: ¿Quieres ir al cine? (Do you want to go to the cinema?)
lessons.try: Plan an outing with a partner.
Role-play a video call with problems.
Two-minute unscripted conversation.

learn: Verbs ending in ar change their ending to match who does the action: hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, hablan.
Hablar (to speak), caminar (to walk), estudiar (to study), bailar (to dance).
Yo hablo español. Nosotros caminamos a la escuela.
lessons.try: Conjugate three ar verbs and use each in a sentence.

learn: Er verbs: como, comes, come, comemos, comen (comer, to eat).
Ir verbs: vivo, vives, vive, vivimos, viven (vivir, to live).
Only the nosotros form is different between er and ir verbs: comemos, vivimos.
lessons.try: Write a paragraph using comer, beber, vivir and escribir.

learn: Some verbs do not follow the pattern. Tener: tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tienen.
Ir (to go): voy, vas, va, vamos, van. Hacer (to do): hago, haces, hace, hacemos, hacen.
Vamos a means let's go or we are going to.
lessons.try: Use voy, tengo and hago in sentences about your weekend.
Conjugate hablar for all subjects.
Conjugate comer and vivir side by side.

learn: Querer: quiero, quieres, quiere, queremos, quieren.
Poder: puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, pueden.
The stem changes except in nosotros.
lessons.try: Sort stem-changing forms.
Say where five people go.

learn: Tengo hambre, tengo sed, tengo frío.
lessons.try: Act out tener expressions.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Present Tense
lessons.try: Verb race game.

learn: Gustar means to be pleasing. Me gusta el chocolate means chocolate is pleasing to me.
Use gusta for one thing or an action, gustan for more than one: me gustan los perros.
Te gusta (you like), le gusta (he or she likes), nos gusta (we like), les gusta (they like).
lessons.try: Write five sentences about what your family likes.

learn: Me encanta means I love it. Me interesa means it interests me. Me molesta means it bothers me.
These work just like gustar: me encantan los libros.
Use them to share opinions with feeling.
lessons.try: Tell three things you love and one that bothers you.

learn: Ask: ¿Qué te gusta más, el fútbol o el béisbol? Más means more.
Count the answers and make a bar graph with Spanish labels.
A mí también means me too. A mí tampoco means me neither.
check: A mí tampoco agrees with a...
lessons.try: Survey ten people and present your graph in Spanish.

learn: Me gustan los libros (more than one).
Gustar agrees with the thing liked.
lessons.try: Write five gustar sentences with singular and plural.

check: Le gusta means he or she...
lessons.try: Ask and report what others like.

check: If a friend says "No me gusta el brócoli" and you agree, say...
lessons.try: Play a "me too, me neither" game.

learn: ¿Qué prefieres, el cine o el parque?
lessons.try: Survey preferences in the class.

learn: Make a mini book: Mis cosas favoritas.
check: A mini book has one page per...
lessons.try: Make a mini book.
Class likes survey presentation.

learn: El avión (plane), el tren (train), el barco (ship), el metro (subway), el taxi.
Viajar means to travel. Viajo en tren means I travel by train.
El aeropuerto, la estación de tren and el puerto are the places they leave from.
lessons.try: Plan a trip and say how you would travel each part.

learn: El boleto is the ticket. El pasaporte is the passport. La maleta is the suitcase.
La salida is the departure or exit. La llegada is the arrival.
¿A qué hora sale el vuelo? asks what time the flight leaves.
lessons.try: Make a pretend boarding pass with Spanish labels.

learn: Ir a plus a verb tells the future: voy a viajar (I am going to travel).
Vamos a visitar a mis abuelos. We are going to visit my grandparents.
Mañana voy a nadar. Tomorrow I am going to swim.
check: Ir a plus a verb tells about the...
lessons.try: Write five plans for next summer with voy a.

check: To travel abroad you need a...
lessons.try: Write a packing list in Spanish.

check: Tengo una reservación means I have a...
lessons.try: Role-play checking in at a hotel.

learn: Sale means leaves; llega means arrives.
lessons.try: Read a Spanish train timetable.

check: Un abrazo at the end means...
lessons.try: Write a postcard from a Spanish-speaking city.

check: On a trip, stay with your...
lessons.try: Make a travel safety card.
Plan a trip itinerary.

learn: ¿Qué te pasa? means what's wrong? Me duele el estómago means my stomach hurts.
Tengo dolor de cabeza (headache), tengo gripe (flu), tengo un resfriado (a cold).
Me siento mal means I feel bad. Me siento mejor means I feel better.
lessons.try: Act out a doctor visit describing three symptoms.

learn: Comer frutas y verduras, beber agua, hacer ejercicio y dormir bien.
Es importante means it is important. Es importante dormir nueve horas.
Debes means you should. Debes lavarte las manos.
lessons.try: Make a health poster with five es importante sentences.

learn: Una curita is a bandage. El hielo is ice. ¡Ayuda! means help!
¡Cuidado! means be careful! Llama al 911 means call 911.
Knowing these words can help someone in an emergency.
lessons.try: Make a first aid kit label list in English and Spanish.
Describe symptoms to a pretend doctor.

check: Debes tomar agua means you should drink...
lessons.try: Give advice for three illnesses.

learn: Dos veces al día (twice a day).
lessons.try: Read a pretend medicine label.
Practise an emergency call script.

learn: Hablo con alguien (I talk to someone).
check: Hablo con alguien means I talk to...
lessons.try: Make a calm-down plan in Spanish.
Doctor visit skit.

learn: El río (river), el lago (lake), la montaña, el valle (valley), el cañón (canyon), el cactus.
El Gran Cañón is in Arizona. El saguaro is the giant cactus of the Sonoran Desert.
lessons.try: Describe a place in nature you have visited.

learn: Apaga la luz (turn off the light). Cierra el agua (turn off the water).
La Tierra is the Earth. Cuidamos la Tierra means we take care of the Earth.
lessons.try: Make a list of five ways your family can cuidar la Tierra.

learn: El agua es preciosa en el desierto. Water is precious in the desert.
La sequía is a drought. La lluvia is rain.
Desert plants store water, and people save water too.
lessons.try: Write three sentences in Spanish about saving water.

learn: Reciclar (to recycle), reutilizar (to reuse), reducir (to reduce).
check: Las tres erres are reduce, reuse and...
lessons.try: Label recycling bins in Spanish.

check: The Sonoran Desert is shared by Arizona and...
lessons.try: Draw a Sonoran Desert scene with Spanish labels.

learn: Cierra la llave (turn off the tap).
lessons.try: Write five water-saving tips.

learn: Hace más calor cada año en muchos lugares.
lessons.try: Discuss three actions to help the planet.

learn: Torres del Paine in Chile, Iguazú Falls in Argentina and Brazil.
lessons.try: Make a brochure for one park.
Green action plan presentation.

learn: To tell what happened, use the past tense. Hablar becomes hablé (I spoke), hablaste, habló, hablamos, hablaron.
Ayer jugué al fútbol. Yesterday I played soccer.
The accent mark shows which part to stress: habló.
lessons.try: Write three things you did yesterday with ar verbs.

lessons.t: The Past with ER and IR Verbs
learn: Comer becomes comí (I ate), comiste, comió, comimos, comieron.
Vivir becomes viví, viviste, vivió, vivimos, vivieron.
Anoche comí pizza. Last night I ate pizza.
lessons.try: Tell a partner what you ate yesterday.

learn: Fui means I went: fui al parque. Fuimos means we went.
El fin de semana pasado means last weekend.
Put it together: El sábado fui al parque y jugué con mi perro.
check: I will go to the park
El fin de semana pasado means...
lessons.try: Write a short paragraph about last weekend.
Make a past-time word wall.

learn: Hice (I did or made), tuve (I had).
Hice la tarea. Tuve un examen.
check: Hice la tarea means I ___ my homework.
Hice and tuve are ___ past verbs.
lessons.try: Tell three things you did and had yesterday.
Interview a partner about their weekend.

learn: Hoy fui al parque. Jugué con mi perro.
check: A diary uses mostly the ___ tense.
lessons.try: Write a diary entry in the past.

learn: El verano pasado visité a mis abuelos.
lessons.try: Tell a partner about last summer.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: The Past
lessons.try: Story of my weekend presentation.

learn: Había una vez means once upon a time. Fin means the end.
El personaje is the character. El lugar is the setting. El problema is the problem.
Stories have un principio (beginning), un medio (middle) and un final (end).
lessons.try: Retell a story you know using había una vez and fin.

learn: An old Aztec legend says a rabbit can be seen on the Moon. Look at the full Moon and you may see its shape.
In the story, a kind rabbit offered itself to feed a hungry traveler. To honor it, the traveler placed its picture on the Moon.
La luna is the Moon. El conejo is the rabbit. Generoso means generous.
check: Where is the rabbit in the legend?
lessons.try: Look at the full Moon and draw the rabbit shape you see.

learn: A fable is a short story with animals and a lesson, called la moraleja.
Use había una vez, past tense verbs and characters with adjectives.
End with: La moraleja es... (the lesson is...).
lessons.try: Write and illustrate a six-sentence fable in Spanish.

learn: A famous legend told in Mexico and the Southwest.
A weeping woman by the river.
Told to keep children away from water at night.
check: She is said to be near a...
lessons.try: Retell the legend in simple Spanish.

learn: Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl stand near Mexico City.
A legend tells of two lovers.
Iztaccíhuatl looks like a sleeping woman.
lessons.try: Draw the two volcanoes.
Match fables to their morals.

learn: Había una vez (once upon a time).
lessons.try: Order picture cards and tell the story.

learn: A famous Spanish novel by Cervantes (1605).
Don Quijote fights windmills he thinks are giants.
check: He fights windmills he thinks are...
lessons.try: Draw Don Quijote and the windmills.
Perform a legend as a play.

learn: Spain is in Europe. Its capital is Madrid. Spanish began there long ago.
Spain has old castles, the Alhambra palace and the famous Sagrada Familia church in Barcelona.
Paella is a rice dish from Valencia, and flamenco is a dance with guitar and clapping.
lessons.try: Listen to flamenco music and clap the rhythm.

learn: Cuba, Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic are Spanish-speaking islands in the Caribbean Sea.
Puerto Rico is part of the United States, and its people are US citizens.
Island music like salsa and merengue is famous for dancing.
lessons.try: Find the three islands on a map and label them.

learn: Más que means more than. Menos que means less than. Tan como means as ... as.
Madrid es más grande que Tucson. Tucson es tan caluroso como Sevilla en el verano.
Comparing helps us see what is the same and different.
lessons.try: Make a Venn diagram comparing your town with a Spanish-speaking city.

learn: Some regions have their own languages.
Catalán and gallego are spoken too.
check: Spain has ___ regions with own languages.
Andalucía is in the ___ of Spain.
lessons.try: Map Spain's regions.

learn: Famous for music like son and salsa.
Old colourful cars on the streets.
check: Salsa is a kind of ___ and dance.
lessons.try: Listen to a son cubano rhythm.

check: The Dominican Republic shares an island with...
lessons.try: Learn a few merengue steps.

learn: Visit the Prado museum in Madrid.
lessons.try: Describe Las Meninas in Spanish.

learn: Not everyone in Spain takes a siesta today.
check: Does everyone in Spain take a siesta?
lessons.try: Find one myth and one fact about Spain.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Spain and the Caribbean
lessons.try: Culture comparison poster.

learn: Pick a topic: a country, a food, a festival or a famous person from a Spanish-speaking country.
Collect five facts. Write each one as a simple sentence in Spanish.
Use words you know, and look up only a few new ones.
check: How many facts should you collect?
lessons.try: Choose your topic and write your five facts.

learn: Add a title, pictures and labels in Spanish.
Practice saying it aloud three times before presenting.
Speak slowly and look at your audience.
lessons.try: Make your poster or slides and practice speaking.

learn: Start with: Buenos días. Hoy voy a hablar de... (today I am going to talk about...).
After, think about what you did well and what you will practice next.
check: Hoy voy a hablar de... means...
Today I am going to talk about...
I do not want to talk
lessons.try: Present your project to your family or class.

learn: Pick a country, a person or a tradition.
Make sure you can find information.
check: A good project starts with a...
A topic can be a ___ or a tradition.
lessons.try: Choose your topic and question.

learn: Write key words, not whole sentences.
lessons.try: Take five notes from a source.

learn: Use present tense and some past.
check: A script has an introduction, facts and a...
lessons.try: Write your presentation script.

learn: Vowels: a, e, i, o, u, always the same sound.
lessons.try: Record yourself and listen back.
Give feedback to two classmates.
Final Spanish presentation.
